Download published references, or the whole database

Source: R/md-fetch.R
md_fetch_reference.Rd

Most users never build matchdb. They download a compiled reference - a few hundred megabytes - and match against it. md_fetch_reference() copies a published bundle from the remote into the local publish directory, where md_reference() reads it; md_reference(fetch = TRUE) does both. md_fetch_db() downloads the full database (about 10 GB) for those who want to compile their own slices with md_spec() and md_compile(), or browse it with md_lookup() and md_cluster(). Between the two, md_fetch_tranches() downloads only the parquet files one spec needs.

Usage

md_fetch_reference(
  label,
  spec_hash = NULL,
  remote = md_remote(),
  root = md_path("publish"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

md_fetch_db(
  remote = md_remote(),
  dest = md_path("db", "MATCHDB.duckdb"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

md_remote()

Arguments

label

A published label: active-legal, active-observed, unified-legal or unified-observed.

spec_hash

A specific bundle; by default the one the remote's latest.json points at.

remote

The base URL of a matchdb copy (holding MATCHDB.duckdb and publish/).

root

The local publish directory.

overwrite

Download again even if the bundle is already here and intact.

dest

Where to put the database. The default is where md_db() looks.

Value

md_fetch_reference(): the local bundle directory, invisibly.

md_fetch_db(): the local database path, invisibly.

The remote

The default is the public NCCS copy, https://nccs-efile.s3.amazonaws.com/dev/matchdb, read over plain HTTPS: no AWS account or credentials are needed. Set options(matchdb.remote = ...) to use another copy; any URL utils::download.file() can read works, including file:// paths.

Every file is checked against the md5 recorded when it was published (the bundle's stamp.json, the database's MANIFEST.json), and a file that does not match is deleted rather than kept.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
md_fetch_reference("active-observed")
b <- md_reference("active-observed")

# or in one step
b <- md_reference("active-observed", fetch = TRUE)
} # }
